method: 3 real extraction-sized calls: system="", user=DEFAULT_NER_PROMPT.replace('{{source}}', <real corpus paragraph>), temperature=0, extra_body={'provider': 'provider-6'}, via palimpsest.llm.client.LLMClient (same client class/User-Agent the harness uses). analysis.interpretation: Near-constant ~4670-4690 hidden prompt tokens regardless of real content size (431-525 words) is the textbook signature of a fixed reseller-padding overhead, not content-proportional tokenization. This matches (and slightly exceeds) the ~4400 tokens/call documented in docs/stages/wiki-eval.md for gpt-5.4-mini on provider-6, and is consistent with the pre-existing 2026-07-05 triage finding for openai/gpt-5.5 itself on provider-6 (docs/experiments/2026-07-05-model-comparison/triage/gpt-5.5.json: 10/10 success, prompt_tokens_median=4395 on a ~10-word probe prompt, verdict='padded', excluded from the eligible-route pool).
analysis.cost_usd_field: null on all 3 calls (provider-6 does not surface real billed cost for this model/route) -- confirmed against the same behavior in the 2026-07-05 triage (cost_source='estimated' for every provider-6/gpt-5.5 call there too). This means BudgetGuard.settle() in scripts/wiki_eval.py, which only updates spend when `actual` (usage.cost_usd) is not None, would NEVER correct its pre-call estimate (EST_COST_PER_EXTRACT_CALL / EST_COST_PER_JUDGE_CALL, built from a 1000-1200 assumed prompt tokens) toward the real ~5650-5863 padded token count -- the $15 cap in the harness would not reliably detect or stop on the true padded spend.
analysis.estimated_smoke_cost_basis: PRICE_TABLE openai/gpt-5.5 = $0.30/$0.30 per Mtok in/out (scripts/probe_providers.py), applied to observed prompt+completion tokens since cost_usd was not surfaced.

decision: Per the owner-locked protocol ("if you observe padding anywhere near that scale for gpt-5.5, STOP and report instead of running"), the full 100-article run was not started.
